items.claim: The row's terminal verse carries the prefixed divine-title stack la-adonai YHWH tsevaot, and the row both suppresses that disclosure and reports a settled byte fact as an open re-derivation question.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.50.25 reads כִּי מְלָאכָ֣ה הִ֗יא לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים (byte tier); the three-element title לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת (byte tier) stands inside the very clause the row makes its closing warrant, and the corresponding rendering at web:Jer.50.25 is “for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans”. The prefixed form is its own token object and is invisible to a bare-token adonai sweep: the bare qamats token stands at 11 verses (sweep: 11 verses, accent-stripped tier, MT keys), while the lamed-prefixed form stands at 2 verses carrying 3 tokens (sweep: 2 verses / 3 tokens, skeleton tier, MT keys), the other site being oshb:Jer.46.10 with two tokens in one verse. The row's device prose states that the clause is not cited as carrying a divine-title stack and that a byte re-derivation question on the point is held elsewhere; the pointed bytes settle it, so a mandated disclosure object present in the row's own final verse is withheld on a stated ground the substrate does not support, and the sentence narrating where the question is held is workflow prose rather than substrate grounds. The row's rationale further flattens the stack to the divine name alone, and the row's evidence refs stop at oshb:Jer.50.24. Disclosure is asymmetric inside this stretch: the postpositive stack at oshb:Jer.50.31 is disclosed four verses on, and the full YHWH tsevaot Elohei Yisrael stack at oshb:Jer.50.18 is disclosed with its digit. The rest of the row verifies: the doubled particle אֵ֤יךְ and אֵ֣יךְ at oshb:Jer.50.23 and the first-person יָקֹ֨שְׁתִּי at oshb:Jer.50.24 both reach byte tier at their cited refs, the voice-turn at 50:24 is byte-true against the impersonal 50:22-23, and the SAMEKH at MT 50:21 named as the front seam is inventory-true (single-witness).

items.claim: The clause the row reads as a closing cap is one half of a two-verse doublet whose other half sits inside the fresh onset four verses on, and that byte-true device straddles the row's own back seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.50.27 closes כִּֽי בָ֥א יוֹמָ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם and oshb:Jer.50.31 closes כִּ֛י בָּ֥א יוֹמְךָ֖ עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיךָ (both byte tier at their cited refs). The paired ki-ba-yom plus visitation shape stands at 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys) and those are the two sites here; the visitation element on its own is common (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys), so the discriminating object is the paired onset, not the visitation noun. The row's warrant for closing at 50:27 rests on reading the hoy plus day-of-visitation clause as capping the imperative already issued, while the same construction four verses on is read as belonging to a fresh challenge onset; neither end discloses the pairing, so a byte-true device crosses this seam without disclosure and argues continuity for the 50:26-32 stretch against the cut. The row's positive grounds otherwise verify: the imperative chain בֹּֽאוּ לָ֤הּ מִקֵּץ֙ פִּתְח֣וּ at oshb:Jer.50.26 and the bare ה֣וֹי עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם at oshb:Jer.50.27 both reach byte tier, the particle's role is split before any digit is taken and is correctly separated from this book's woe-oracle onsets and funeral-cry uses, and the SAMEKH at MT 50:27 named as the row's close is inventory-true (single-witness).

items.claim: The shared closing formula's other site is assigned to the wrong nation oracle: by its own header bytes that verse stands inside the Damascus unit, not the Ammon unit, and the row leaves the second inventory entry in the verse it engages undisclosed.
items.evidence: The formula match itself is byte-true: לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ reaches byte tier at both oshb:Jer.50.30 and oshb:Jer.49.26 and stands at 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys), and the two differences the row names verify — אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתָּ֥הּ against אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה, and נְאֻם יְהוָֽה against נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (byte tier at their refs). The attribution does not: the lamed header at oshb:Jer.49.23 reads לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק, the next lamed header is לְקֵדָ֣ר וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר at oshb:Jer.49.28, and oshb:Jer.49.27 kindles fire בְּחוֹמַ֣ת דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק — so 49:26 sits inside the Damascus unit, while the Ammon header is לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן at oshb:Jer.49.1 (all byte tier). The same body of work reads 49:24 as Damascus and 49:5 as Ammon, so the assignment is internally inconsistent as well as byte-refuted, and it is doing shared-texture work in the row's own closing warrant. Second defect: MT 50:29 carries both a ketiv/qere entry and a paseq entry in the single-witness inventory; the row engages one and leaves the other unstated, so span-relevant mark symmetry stays open in the very verse it engages, and it also ties the ketiv/qere to a named word, which a per-verse-count inventory cannot source. The onset splice ק֥וֹל נָסִ֛ים וּפְלֵטִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ בָּבֶ֑ל reaches byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.28, and the row correctly treats that verse as a verbless report rather than an imperative, keeping the seam argument off the English rendering.

items.claim: The row's count for the neum adonai YHWH tsevaot stack is wrong and undigited: the full stack stands at three verses book-wide, not two, and no scope is stated that would exclude the third.
items.evidence: The splices verify: הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ זָד֔וֹן and נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת both reach byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.31, and the match to oshb:Jer.49.5 holds at accent-stripped tier. The count does not. The full stack stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys): oshb:Jer.2.19 closes נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת, differing from the row's own site by the final accent alone, alongside oshb:Jer.49.5 and oshb:Jer.50.31. The row states the site is the second of two such sites, a bare count that names neither a sweep digit nor a scope, so an exclusivity count is asserted that the bytes refute; a tier label on the splice does not stand in for the sweep. The shorter stack lacking tsevaot at oshb:Jer.2.22, נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (byte tier), is a further object the row's count does not separate. The same body of work elsewhere gives a named object and a digit for a divine-title-stack count, so the standard was available. The rejected alternative's claim that this book opens fresh units with the same challenge shape is byte-supportable but likewise undigited (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys — oshb:Jer.21.13, oshb:Jer.50.31, oshb:Jer.51.25). Both seam marks the row names, MT 50:30 and MT 50:32, are inventory-true (single-witness).

items.claim: The row's lawsuit-root argument, which carries its unit-type reasoning, is made in transliteration rather than on the pointed bytes and carries neither a spliced form nor a tier label, and the row leaves the paseq entry inside its own span undisclosed while engaging a parashah mark at its front seam.
items.evidence: The onset verifies: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת reaches byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.33 with the frame owner named inside the formula itself rather than left to inference, and גֹּאֲלָ֣ם חָזָ֗ק יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שְׁמ֔וֹ reaches byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.34; the SAMEKH at MT 50:32 named as the front seam is inventory-true (single-witness). Two gaps. First, the splice stops at the divine-name clause, and the argument that follows — the root identity with this book's trial-speech material, and the intensive reading behind the rendering — is stated in transliteration alone, lacking a pointed run and lacking a tier, although the run רִ֥יב יָרִ֖יב אֶת רִיבָ֑ם (byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.34) stands in the same verse and would carry the infinitive-absolute reading on the bytes; the root's spread is also undigited (sweep: 10 verses / 13 tokens, skeleton tier, MT keys), and with no morphology layer staged a form-class claim needs the pointed bytes rather than a transliteration. Second, MT 50:34 carries a paseq entry in the single-witness inventory; the row engages a parashah mark at its front seam and discloses no mark object inside the span it cuts, leaving span-relevant symmetry open. The row's back seam also carries an undisclosed catchword: לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל closes oshb:Jer.50.34 and וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל opens the next verse's list (byte tier at their refs) — one edit cures it at both ends of that seam.

items.claim: The pointed wordplay is byte-exact as argued, but a construct chain attested at 3 verses book-wide stands on both sides of the row's own front seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The wordplay claim verifies at codepoint level: חֶ֥רֶב at oshb:Jer.50.35 and חֹ֥רֶב at oshb:Jer.50.38 (both byte tier) share the same consonantal skeleton and the same accent and differ in the first vowel alone, segol against holam, so the row's pointing-alone reading is exact; the accent-stripped tier separates the two words while the skeleton tier does not, and the litany runs 5 sword tokens over 50:35-37 against 1 drought token at 50:38 (sweep: 6 tokens over 4 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys). Holding this pair apart from the catalogued call-vision pun is correct, and the anaphora argument does not depend on the English. The gap is at the front seam: the construct chain yoshvei-Bavel stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys — oshb:Jer.50.34, oshb:Jer.50.35, oshb:Jer.51.12), and two of those three are the verses immediately either side of this row's opening, לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל closing oshb:Jer.50.34 against וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל inside oshb:Jer.50.35 (byte tier). A byte-true catchword hook across the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and the row records a scene shift at that point without engaging it. A secondary looseness: the sword is said to be repeated against a six-item list, but the princes and wise men of 50:35 are governed by the prepositional chain, not by a repeated sword token.

items.claim: The three-verse digit is right but it is attached to the wrong object: the row calls this site a third occurrence of the Sodom-and-Gomorrah refrain when one of the three counted verses carries no Sodom, no Gomorrah and no overthrow noun.
items.evidence: The byte claim holds exactly: לֹֽא יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן אָדָֽם stands at byte tier in 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, byte tier, MT keys — oshb:Jer.49.18, oshb:Jer.49.33, oshb:Jer.50.40), and the device prose scopes that count correctly. The rationale then labels the counted object differently. oshb:Jer.49.33 opens וְהָיְתָ֨ה חָצ֜וֹר לִמְע֥וֹן תַּנִּ֛ים שְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד עוֹלָ֑ם (byte tier) and carries none of the three elements the label names: the kaph-prefixed overthrow noun stands at 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys — כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת at oshb:Jer.49.18 and כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים at oshb:Jer.50.40, both byte tier), and the same skeleton at 3 further verses is the article-bearing stocks noun, a homograph outside this object. The two overthrow verses are not byte-identical to each other either: oshb:Jer.50.40 adds the divine noun and the object markers and closes נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה against אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier). The book's third Sodom verse, oshb:Jer.23.14, reads כִּסְדֹ֔ם וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כַּעֲמֹרָֽה (byte tier) — a kaph-prefixed comparison of persons, not a member of the overthrow object. Naming the counted object as the Sodom-and-Gomorrah refrain while counting the closing clause blends two classes at the row's own closing warrant; the cure is to name the swept object before the count and keep the two digits apart. The onset splice לָכֵ֗ן יֵשְׁב֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת אִיִּ֔ים reaches byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.39. The declared heuristic false positive on this row is CONFIRMED: the flagged word there is an ordinary adjective inside a rejected-tiling sentence and asserts nothing exclusive that would need a sweep digit beside it.
